newsitem.title: GERMANY: Young German CDU leader opposes tax hikes.
newsitem.headline: Young German CDU leader opposes tax hikes.

text.p: A prominent young leader of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) urged the German government in an interview on Tuesday not to raise taxes to fill huge gaps in its 1997 budget.

Christian Wulff, CDU leader in Lower Saxony state and one of the most outspoken up-and-coming leaders in the party, said Finance Minister Theo Waigel should slash state spending rather than increase taxes as he is reportedly planning to do.
Kohl's pro-business Free Democratic (FDP) coalition partners have been stonewalling against tax increases but Wulff was the first CDU leader to speak out against a hike.
"The tax burden has reached the maximum point for achievers and skilled workers in this society," Wulff told the Chemnitz daily Freie Presse.
He said welfare spending had gone up by 33 percent since 1991 while gross domestic product rose by 21 percent, net wages by 18 percent and investment by only 14 percent.
"Something is wrong in this country," said Wulff.

Wulff, 37, known as one of the "wild youngsters" in the CDU, said tensions in Kohl's coalition between his party and its liberal Free Democrats (FDP) reminded him of 1966, when the last CDU-FDP coalition collapsed over a tax dispute.
"The situation is extraordinarily serious," he said, adding that a quick solution in differences over the 1998 budget would not solve the whole problem.
"Just cutting through the know will not banish the crisis," he said. "This country has become too cumbersome and awkward."
